Targets for a project dictionary

Source: R/targets.R
tar_dict.Rd

tar_dict() makes a targets pipeline depend on the entries of dict.yml it reads, and on nothing else in the file. It returns the targets dict_file (the file), dict_values (the dictionary as read_dict() reads it) and dict_<key> (the value of each entry), and attaches the dictionary as the object dict on the search path, as weft:dict, so that commands and functions in the pipeline find it (rule 4.6.1). Pass the result of the pipeline's targets to tar_dict_deps(), which adds to each target the entries it reads. A changed value then re-runs exactly the targets that read it, and a changed definition, a new key or a reordered file re-runs none (rule 4.6.3).

Usage

tar_dict(path = "dict.yml")

Arguments

path

The dictionary file, one string.

Value

A list of target objects.

Details

Do not define dict in _targets.R: targets would track the whole object, and every reader would re-run when any entry changed. That is an error.

Limit: dict is attached in the session that defines the pipeline. A parallel crew worker does not have it, so a function that reads dict fails there with "object 'dict' not found". Pass the values the function needs as arguments, or run the pipeline without workers.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# _targets.R
library(targets)
c(
  weft::tar_dict("dict.yml"),
  weft::tar_dict_deps(list(
    tar_target(limit_ok, dict$limit > 3)
  ))
)
} # }
